title: Validation of a New Sampler for Radon Gas Measurements in Surface Water
author: Luís, Pereira, et al.

steps.title: Assemble sampler and accessories
steps.instruction: Gather the metallic 1 L bottle‑shaped sampler, its lever‑spring lid mechanism, two weight messengers, a metric rope, optional extra weights, a diode fishing light, a tygon tube, a gas‑tight syringe, a pre‑filled LSC Teflon vial and Betaplate Scint scintillation cocktail.

steps.title: Attach depth‑indicator light (optional)
steps.instruction: Clip the diode light to the lid level; when the lid contacts water the light flashes, allowing visual confirmation of depth.

steps.title: Lower sampler to target depth
steps.instruction: From a high point (e.g., bridge) lower the sampler attached to the rope; feel the tension when the lid touches the water surface, then continue lowering until the desired depth is reached while keeping the sampler watertight.

steps.title: Open sampler at depth
steps.instruction: Drop the first weight messenger down the rope; this triggers the lever that opens the lid, allowing water to enter the sampler.

steps.title: Fill sampler for calibrated time
steps.instruction: Allow the sampler to fill for approximately one and a half minutes (≈ 90 s).

steps.title: Close sampler and retrieve
steps.instruction: Drop the second weight messenger; this activates the closing lever, sealing the sampler. Then lift the sampler back to the operator.

steps.title: Collect water sample with syringe
steps.instruction: Connect the gas‑tight syringe to the sampler via the tygon tube and withdraw 10 mL of water from inside the sampler.

steps.title: Transfer water to LSC vial
steps.instruction: Inject the 10 mL water into a pre‑prepared LSC Teflon vial that already contains an immiscible scintillation cocktail (Betaplate Scint).

steps.title: Seal, shake and rest vial
steps.instruction: Seal the vial tightly, shake vigorously to promote radon extraction into the cocktail, then let the vial rest undisturbed for at least 3 hours to allow ^222Rn to reach secular equilibrium with its short‑lived progeny before counting.
